title: EWG's 2026 Shopper's Guide to Pesticides in Produce: Summary
summary: EWG's 2026 Dirty Dozen and Clean Fifteen rankings from USDA residue data, highlighting PFAS pesticides and mixture risks.

assertions.quote: Shoppers who want to reduce their exposure to pesticides can consider buying organic versions of produce on the Dirty Dozen, when possible.
organic produce is often a good way to reduce pesticide exposure
When regulators consider health harms from pesticide exposure, they assess the substances one at a time.
A diet that is high in fruit and vegetables, whether organic or conventional, is important for health.
levels of exposure once considered safe by the Environmental Protection Agency were in fact set too high
The most frequently detected pesticides on all fruits and vegetables, and three of the 10 most frequently detected pesticides, are PFAS pesticides.

verdicts.note: Fludioxonil, fluopyram and bifenthrin carry fluorinated groups meeting the OECD PFAS definition, though their risk differs from legacy PFAS.

EWG's tally of USDA data finds fludioxonil (14% of samples), fluopyram (8%) and bifenthrin (7%), all meeting the international PFAS definition, among the ten most detected pesticides, with fludioxonil the most detected overall; the counts are data, the PFAS framing is EWG's.

assertions.quote: the guide aims to provide useful information about how to reduce exposure to pesticides – particularly for more vulnerable groups, including young children
